after:
The original-split representation comparison uses raw ESM, full FPP, ablated FPP (three fits each) and three topology permutations by three seeds (nine fits). Original-split fusion uses score-only, raw, full and ablated arms (three fits each) plus permuted fusion (nine). Homology fusion uses score-only, raw and full FPP (three fits each). Score-only and fusion models use the same hidden-layer architecture, but score-only models have fewer input-layer parameters. The matched STRING experiments comprise 81 distinct condition–seed combinations: the 48 core comparisons above, 27 partial-ablation interior fits and six homology-aware representation fits. Six additional full-graph/fully ablated endpoint fits bring the total to 87 fitting executions. The three frozen-full positive controls reproduced their saved metrics and selected epochs. Sparse GPU propagation was not bitwise reproducible across repeated evaluations. We retained the first regenerated fully ablated tensor and its first three fits, froze their checksums and checked the propagation independently in float64 on the CPU in 16 columns. These fully ablated fits differ numerically from the archived fits and supply both Figure 1D and the shared fraction-1 endpoint in Figure 1E. Diagnostic regenerations were excluded from training. The full-graph endpoint is likewise shared across strategies. The additional fits used the same Python and numerical-library versions in a separate runtime: 122 exported pip-package pins and 16 portable conda-library pins were verified, together with pip, setuptools and wheel, for 141 verified package versions. Input checksums, frozen node order, all sample labels and split memberships, homology-cluster disjointness, and the full-graph propagation calculation were verified before fitting. No ESM extraction or homology clustering was repeated. Partial ablation retained 621,211 eligible undirected train-test pairs (1,242,422 edge entries) with complete STRING score coverage; each selected pair was removed in both directions, followed by recomputation of normalized propagation. The 25%, 50% and 75% conditions removed 155,303, 310,606 and 465,908 pairs, respectively. Graph masks were fixed independently of test labels, and every classifier was selected only by validation AUC.

before: **Unified current reporting.** Tables 11–17, the current matched results reported in the main text and the external/network comparisons in main Figure 5 use a single post-processing convention. For all 21 protein-only representation checkpoints, CPU evaluation in float32 with fixed batches of 1,024 nodes in the frozen node order produces one stored probability per protein, which is mapped to its variant rows. On the original validation/test rows, the largest difference from the earlier variant-batched probabilities was 3.58e-7; the maximum within-protein spread decreased from 2.38e-7 to exactly zero. Fusion inputs remain variant-specific. Seed probabilities are converted to float64 before averaging; all AUPRC values are non-interpolated average precision computed consistently with scikit-learn. This inference and aggregation standardization involved no model refitting or checkpoint changes. It can slightly change rank-based metrics through exact ties; earlier outputs remain archived separately rather than mixed with the current tables.
after: **Unified reporting.** Tables 11–17 and main Figures 1B–F, 2B–E, 3B–F, 4 and 5 use the same inference and aggregation convention. For protein-only representation models, CPU evaluation in float32 with fixed batches of 1,024 nodes in the frozen node order produces one probability per protein, which is mapped to its variant rows. Fusion inputs remain variant-specific. Seed probabilities are converted to float64 before averaging, and AUPRC is calculated as non-interpolated average precision. Per-run means and sample standard deviations summarize individual classifier metrics; ensemble differences are calculated after averaging probabilities. The original reporting audit covered 21 representation checkpoints: on the original validation/test rows, the largest change from variant-batched probabilities was 3.58e-7 and the maximum within-protein spread decreased from 2.38e-7 to exactly zero. The 39 additional fitting executions use the same node-wise inference convention, with every mapped validation/test probability checked against the saved variant-batched output within 2e-6. The homology representation interval uses 2,000 paired protein-clustered resamples of the full-FPP and raw-ESM ensembles (Table 12), conditional on the fitted models and fixed graph. These intervals omit retraining and graph-sampling uncertainty and are not adjusted for multiple comparisons.
